string.text: An exceptionally rare and outrageously expensive cartridge with monstrous stopping power. Its heavy bullet can stop even a charging boar or snork in its tracks, but the thick lead core performs poorly against body armor plates.

The most common and dirt-cheap cartridge in the Zone. Ideal for culling tushkanos, blind dogs, and bandits in leather jackets—provided they aren't wearing chainmail. Virtually useless against armor plates and thick-skinned mutants.

An overpressured, high-pressure round. Deals increased flesh damage and allows for a better defense against mutant packs, though the caliber remains rather weak and even then barely catches up to 9x19 Parabellum.

A common Western-standard cartridge popular among mercenaries and seasoned stalkers. More accurate and harder-hitting than Soviet 9x18, well-suited for small and medium creatures, but falters against military body armor.
Hollow-point expanding round. Expands violently upon impact to tear soft tissue, making it a great choice against unarmored flesh, though any body armor negates this effect almost entirely.

Heavy, large-caliber cartridge. Boasts superior close-range stopping power, easily knocking boars and snorks off their feet, but suffers from one of the steepest ballistic trajectories and low effective range.
An expensive specialty hollow-point cartridge. A true nightmare for small, unarmored mutants and lightly dressed stalkers. Virtually useless against a well-equipped fighter.

Every stalker's best friend when facing the fauna of the Zone. Point-blank lead buckshot is guaranteed to wipe out a small pack of tushkanos or a leaping snork. Barely effective against armored targets.
A solid lead slug that turns a shotgun into a serious mid-range weapon. Even if it fails to pierce armor, it delivers severe blunt-force trauma that will sooner or later prove fatal to the target.

The Zone's primary assault rifle round, standard issue for the Military and Duty faction. A great balance of accuracy and lethality: punches through light body armor and reliably drops medium-sized mutants.

Military armor-piercing cartridge with a hardened alloy core. Indispensable for raids towards the center of the Zone: easily penetrates military combat suits and significantly damages even heavy exoskeletons.

Good old assault rifle cartridge with a lead core. Thanks to its heavy bullet, it packs serious stopping power and penetrates light cover. Favored by veterans for its widespread availability and reliability in firefights.
Armor-piercing variant of the Soviet caliber. Enormous kinetic energy coupled with an armor-piercing core makes this cartridge lethal even against fighters in heavy assault armored suits.
Primary cartridge for Western weapons, widely used by the Freedom faction and Mercenaries. Boasts high velocity and tight grouping, allowing for precise fire on weak spots at long range.
NATO armor-piercing round. High velocity and a specialized penetrator core provide excellent penetration, effectively neutralizing heavily armored hostiles in SEVA suits and exoskeletons.

Belt-fed rifle-grade ammunition. Used in standard Soviet machine guns for suppression fire and clearing mutant dens. These bullets shred incoming waves of biomass and punch straight through thin metal sheets and occasional brick cover.
High-precision sniper round with a steel core. The weapon of choice for Freedom snipers and lone stalkers: a single well-placed shot can decide the outcome of an engagement at extreme range.
Elite armor-piercing sniper round with enhanced grouping. Guaranteed to pierce armored helmets and heavy protection even at extreme ranges, leaving the target no chance.

Heavy subsonic sniper round. Designed for suppressed weapons: maintains excellent grouping and solid stopping power, allowing the shooter to silently drop sentries and eliminate sleeping mutants without unnecessary noise.
Specialized subsonic armor-piercing cartridge. The massive hardened bullet shatters high-grade body armor, enabling silent yet devastating close-quarters combat.
Rare imported PDW cartridge. The pointed bullet reaches high velocities, inflicting severe hydrodynamic trauma on living targets. Perfect for agile kiting and picking off fast mutants.
Military armor-piercing cartridge with a steel penetrator. Thanks to extreme velocity, bursts of this ammunition rip through Kevlar and light stalker suits at close range.

Simple and inexpensive pistol ammunition. Due to its high velocity and bottlenecked casing, the bullet easily penetrates bandit leather jackets and military helmets, though it falls short of larger calibers in mutant-stopping power.
Power cells utilizing unknown anomalous compounds as an energy source. Manufactured in industrial-grade laboratory conditions in the Zone.
Reduced-capacity power cells assembled by local craftsmen from scrap. They utilize artifact fragments to store and discharge energy.
The most common pistol in the Zone, a relic of the Soviet era. The PM is exceptionally reliable, simple to use and maintain, but has a low magazine capacity and poor accuracy.
An engraved PMm awarded to Degtyarev. Bearing the state coat of arms, the inscription reads: "For the successful execution of exceptionally dangerous assignments".
A suppressed pistol developed from the PM for intelligence services. Considered obsolete, but in skilled hands it remains a very effective tool.
A Ukrainian-made pistol. Boasts better accuracy, ergonomics, and magazine capacity compared to the PM.
A modernized variant of the classic Belgian pistol. Despite its age, it remains very popular both worldwide and across the Zone.
Pistols of this series are renowned for their reliability, if somewhat bulky frame. Popular due to their solid caliber and generous magazine capacity.
An excellent Western pistol featuring high reliability, high magazine capacity, and arguably best-in-class ergonomics.
An upgraded version of the legendary classic. Its modest magazine capacity is the only drawback, easily offset by the hard-hitting .45 caliber.
Known for great ergonomics and pinpoint shot placement. In steady demand among veteran stalkers and mercenaries.
A unique SIG Sauer P220. Features an extended magazine, high-durability steel barrel, and a polymer frame.
Renowned for supreme reliability and durability combined with excellent accuracy. A staple among Zone veterans.
A compact high-caliber pistol with a lightened slide. Reportedly once belonged to the mercenary known as Wolfhound.
A literal hand cannon: massive, heavy, and packing terrifying firepower. Rarely seen due to its exorbitant price and sheer weight.
A fairly rare custom Desert Eagle. Precision-machined parts and an extended barrel deliver unprecedented accuracy.
A submachine gun renowned for its reliability and precision. Used by mercenaries and seasoned stalkers to clear tight spaces.
A unique custom piece retrofitted by a gunsmith on order for a mob boss, enabling this weapon to fire cheap Soviet pistol rounds.
A compact bullpup submachine gun with great ergonomics, a high rate of fire, and a generous 50-round magazine.
A sawn-off hunting shotgun. The primary weapon of rookies and bandits: cheap, easy to conceal, and lethal with buckshot at point-blank range.
An over-and-under sawn-off shotgun. Easy to conceal under a coat to avoid questions from passing military patrols.
An over-and-under double-barrel hunting shotgun. Good spread and stopping power provide dependable defense against low-tier mutants.
A widespread side-by-side shotgun. A time-tested, straightforward tool actively used by stalkers on the Zone's outskirts.
A pump-action shotgun. In huge demand thanks to its reliable action and swift cycling speed.
A custom-built pump shotgun once owned by the hunter Trapper. Capable of dropping the toughest mutant with a single well-aimed blast.
A semi-automatic combat shotgun. Known for great reliability and high volume of fire. A formidable, if heavy, weapon for hunting dangerous predators.
An assault modification featuring automatic fire capability and significantly reduced felt recoil.
A combat revolving shotgun. Its main perk is a huge 12-round drum; the downsides are hefty bulk and a painfully slow reload.
A custom piece built for a mercenary contractor. Boasts incredible penetration and muzzle energy at the cost of excessive weight.
A shortened carbine indispensable in cramped tunnels and bunkers. Its stubby barrel yields poor effective range and overheats rapidly during sustained bursts.
A modified AKS-74U sporting a polymer handguard and extended magazine. Formerly belonged to the stalker known as Snag.
The iconic domestic 5.45 mm assault rifle. The Zone's trusty workhorse: unaffected by harsh conditions and easy to maintain.
A variant of the ubiquitous rifle with a side-folding metal stock, convenient for long marches and transport.
An upgraded version with ergonomic controls, a lightened handguard, and tuned internal parts to mitigate recoil.
A modernized general-issue rifle featuring high-impact polymer furniture and a folding stock.
A folding-stock 7.62 mm rifle. A hard-hitting and rugged gun favored by veterans for its heavy punch against large mutants and reliability during continuous fire.
A complex rifle featuring a recoil-delayed blowback system. In 2-round burst mode, both bullets hit virtually the exact same spot, punching through sturdy body armor.
An assault rifle with exceptional grouping and gentle recoil. However, maintenance costs run high due to its scarcity in the Zone.
A British bullpup rifle fitted with factory iron sights. Quite accurate when fired in moderation, but the mechanism jams easily under intense field use.
A top-tier German export rifle. Comes with iron sights and a Picatinny carry handle.
A premier piece of German engineering: lightweight, reliable, and ergonomic, held in high regard by Freedom fighters and mercenaries.
One of the finest assault rifles in the Zone. Combines the surgical accuracy of Western platforms with AK-like mechanical reliability.
Thoroughly disassembled and hand-tuned. The stock is neatly carved with the letter "S" and six small crosses.
A high-tech assault weapon system complete with an integrated optic and underslung grenade launcher. The weapon of the Zone's true elite.
An FN F2000 modification using wear-resistant polyamides. A re-tuned gas block significantly increases bullet muzzle velocity.
A suppressed assault rifle for special forces. Paired with 9x39 mm ammo, it silently dispatches targets in high-tier body armor.
A formidable modular bullpup weapon system with an integrated grenade launcher. Cherished by Duty assault squads for compactness and raw close-range punch.
A prototype upgraded specifically for Zone operations, sporting a rare extended magazine.
A legendary silenced sniper rifle with an integral suppressor. Allows stalkers to land lethal shots from ambush with zero flash and minimal sound.
A custom VSS build. A lower rate of fire is offset by match-grade barrel rifling and monstrous penetration.
A simpler and more pragmatic counterpart to the Vintorez. Easier to keep running, as far as that goes for such an exotic caliber.
A bullpup sniper rifle fitted with a muzzle brake. Much more compact than the SVD, making it ideal for mobile skirmishes.
A shortened sniper rifle capable of full-auto fire. Formerly belonged to Max, Freedom's quartermaster.
A legendary military sniper rifle. The punch of its full-power cartridge drops exo-suited fighters and tears through thick mutant hides at extreme range.
A hand-assembled, precision-built SVDS variant. Its match barrel delivers benchmark sniper accuracy.
A light machine gun based on the AKM, featuring a reinforced receiver and extended heavy barrel. Delivers sustained bursts of heavy, reliable 7.62 mm fire.
A heavy belt-fed machine gun. The ultimate argument for holding back mutant swarms and clearing fortified bases.
An upgraded machine gun belonging to the Duty warrior Zulu. Features an expanded ammo box and heavy-duty feed mechanism for uninterrupted suppression.
The top-secret 'Item 62'. An electromagnetic rail system accelerates projectiles to hypervelocity, erasing any target in line of sight.
An anti-tank rocket launcher. Used in the Zone as an extreme countermeasure against super-predators or during all-out faction wars.
A heavy revolving grenade launcher firing Soviet VOG-25 rounds, occasionally surfacing here and there in single copies.
An unidentified artifact-based weapon whose mechanism remains a mystery. It is clearly broken.
A rapid-firing automatic pistol with a 20-round magazine. Given enough skill and experience managing its wild recoil, it can sub in for an SMG against small mutant ambushes.
A semi-automatic magazine-fed shotgun based on the Kalashnikov receiver. Rapid box magazine swaps make it one of the premier survival shotguns in the Zone.
A semi-automatic DMR built on the LR-300 with an extended match barrel, allowing the user to pick off distant weak points with standard NATO ammunition.
A time-tested bolt-action rifle. Renowned for its sheer reliability and the devastating power of the full-sized 7.62x54mm rifle cartridge.
An improved RPK chambered in 5.45 mm, featuring polymer furniture, a folding stock, and reduced recoil during sustained bursts.
A modernized Makarov pistol featuring improved grip panels, a reinforced frame rated for high-pressure ammunition, and an expanded 12-round magazine.
A domestic military pistol chambered in 9x19 mm. Noted for its light weight and generous capacity, but burdened with a gritty trigger pull and sensitivity to dirt.
The renowned Austrian polymer pistol. A prized find for any stalker: reliable, lightweight, comfortable, and crucially easy to maintain.
A compact carbine chambered in heavy 9x39 mm, mechanically close to the AKS-74U. Combines tight dimensions with the crushing punch of a heavy bullet.
A compact bullpup carbine refined under the A2 modernization program. Nimble in tight corridors and noticeably more reliable than its predecessors.
A service pistol with an extended barrel and suppressor threads, originally conceived for a different caliber.
A shortened tactical carbine variant of the SIG rifle. An ideal pick for mercenaries clearing enclosed spaces due to great handling and rate of fire.
A compact carbine chambered in 9x39 mm without an integral suppressor. Features a very high rate of fire, serving as an aggressive room-clearer.
A British light support weapon with a heavy, lengthened barrel and bipod; in the Zone, it is typically employed as a dedicated mid-range designated marksman rifle.
A powerful pistol chambered in an almost rifle-grade cartridge with a remarkably flat trajectory.
Seized adjustment turrets, warped mounting rail, cloudy glass. Entirely unfit for service, useful only to pawn off to traders for spare change.
A classic optical sight for side dovetail mounts. Fits most domestic assault rifles and sniper systems.
A simple, rugged 3.5x sight. Easily absorbs the recoil of full-power rifle rounds and secures neatly onto matching vintage rails.
A specialized PSO variant featuring an elevation cam calibrated to the steep trajectory of heavy subsonic 9x39 mm rounds.
A rugged British 4x optical sight built for weapons with proprietary dovetail mounts.
A SUSAT sight equipped with a custom adapter allowing installation on standard Picatinny rails.
A high-grade optical sight offering a generous field of view and high-visibility reticle. Mounts to Picatinny rails.
Standard optical sight for the RPG-7 launcher, complete with rangefinder markings for hitting armored targets and clusters of hostiles.
Heavily used in the past and visibly busted. Packed with rust and carbon build-up; stripped threads make it impossible to mount.
Factory expansion chamber attachment for the PB pistol. Ensures whisper-quiet cycling.
A massive suppressor for SVD rifles. Engineered to endure the extreme muzzle pressures of the 7.62x54mm caliber.
Standard-issue sound suppressor for 9A-91 carbines and VSK-94 rifles. Muffles the report of heavy subsonic rounds to a whisper.
Proprietary sound suppressor engineered specifically for the OTs-14 Groza weapon system.
Factory suppressor for the APB machine pistol. Allows quiet, rapid burst fire at close quarters.
Quick-detach NATO suppressor that mounts directly onto the factory flash hider of G36 series rifles.
Imported 1/2x28 threaded suppressor. Compatible with most Western 5.56 mm assault rifles.
Tactical suppressor with M24x1.5 right-hand threads, compatible with most modern 5.45 mm Kalashnikov rifles.
A classic Soviet suppressor with M14x1 left-hand threads, designed for 7.62x39 mm weapons.
A lightweight suppressor threaded for .578x28 UNEF, designed for large-caliber .45 ACP handguns.
A compact pistol suppressor threaded 1/2x28, fitting the vast majority of Western 9x19 mm handguns.
A proprietary suppressor with M12x1 left-hand threads, built specifically for the Fort-14TP pistol.
Underslung grenade launcher for AK-series rifles. Allows the user to lob a VOG-25 round through a window or into a charging pack of mutants.
An American 40mm underslung launcher for Western-pattern rifles. Essential for rooting out fortified enemies.
Grenade launcher module engineered exclusively for the OTs-14 Groza weapon complex.
An offensive hand grenade with a small fragmentation radius. Ideal for room clearing and tight basements without risk to the thrower.
A defensive "lemon" grenade. The cast-iron body generates a lethal storm of heavy shrapnel. Best thrown strictly from solid cover.
Produces a dense wall of grey smoke in seconds, allowing you to reposition under sniper fire or break contact with pursuers.
Fragmentation round for GP-series underslung launchers. Pepper-sprays enemy positions with shrapnel at medium range.
A 40mm high-explosive round for NATO underslung launchers. Packs a concentrated blast at the point of impact.
A fragmentation anti-personnel warhead for the RPG-7 ("pencil"). Designed to wipe out entrenched infantry and dangerous mutants in the open.
